policy: Qt and Kiwix Apple community translations are preserved by exact English source match; Qt wins duplicate sources, followed by non-fuzzy Apple entries. Pinned non-fuzzy Android community imports in community-provenance.json fill remaining exact-source gaps and survive explicit refresh with their per-message provenance. Community attribution is not language competence or context review. Explicit reviewed input must bind the canonical locale, exact English source, exact text/forms, application context, translator, separate reviewer, competence and public HTTPS evidence; it takes precedence over unreviewed imports on every generation/refresh. A reviewed flag alone grants no authority. qqq is documentation, not a runtime locale. Default generation uses bundled inherited data and locale metadata only, excluding pinned fuzzy imports. Missing translations explicitly fall back to English. Count messages require every Intl.PluralRules cardinal category for the locale; flat inherited plurals are not reported as category-complete. Build-time machine translations identify their service in machine.json and plural-translations.json and remain unreviewed unless separately attributable review evidence is supplied. Coverage measures UI source availability, not linguistic quality. Intl formatting uses the host ICU data. StreetZim maps run on Windows, macOS and Linux. No runtime translation requests.

upstream.android: Pinned exact English source matches for partial locales; see community-provenance.json (GPL-3.0-or-later, attribution and source URLs). Bundled in inherited.json; no network required at runtime.
